chunks: 23 - Sa'd narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, from Abū al-Hasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام:
"Abū al-Hasan عليه السلام, when he became distressed, would leave the fifty."
His statement عليه السلام, "he left the fifty," means the completion of the fifty, because the obligatory prayers are not permissible to leave in any circumstance, and this clarifies that.

key_terms.الْخَمْسِينَ: the fifty prayers, referring to the total including obligatory and recommended prayers

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام leaving "the fifty" prayers mean?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Abū al-Hasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام would omit part of the set of fifty prayers when distressed. The accompanying explanation clarifies that what was left was the completion of the fifty, meaning the supererogatory prayers, since the obligatory prayers may never be abandoned under any condition.
